source: Camposampiero et al. (2025) Can Large Reasoning Models do Analogical Reasoning under Perceptual Uncertainty?
finding: First test of reasoning models (o3-mini, DeepSeek R1) on symbolic Raven-style analogy. Strong on the standard set, near chance when the task gets longer, wider in range and noisy.
numbers: o3-mini (medium) full-task accuracy 86.6 on I-RAVEN; 77.6 and 81.0 on two wider-range I-RAVEN-X columns; 17.0 with confounders plus smoothing at max level (chance 12.5); reasoning tokens 7209 -> 18589 as noise rises. R1: 80.6 on I-RAVEN -> about 22.8-23.2 in the hardest setting. o3-mini high effort on the hardest setting only 31.0 at 53596 tokens. Neuro-symbolic ARLC 98.6 -> 88.0.
limits: Symbolic matrices, not far-source verbal analogy. Does not test ARN or letter strings directly.
agent_relevance: Reasoning models do not close the out-of-distribution analogy gap by thinking longer: more tokens did not rescue accuracy. Do not count on extra reasoning to fix far analogy; add structure or tools.

source: Camposampiero et al. (2025) I-RAVEN-X: Benchmarking Generalization and Robustness of Analogical and Mathematical Reasoning in LLMs and LRMs
finding: Reasoning models beat plain LLMs on longer rules and wider value ranges, but still fail under perceptual uncertainty.
numbers: Arithmetic accuracy 80.5 -> 63.0 for LRMs vs 59.3 -> 4.4 for LLMs as range grows. Task accuracy under uncertainty drops by 61.8 points for LRMs.
limits: Abstract and tables read; symbolic analogies only. Workshop-level paper.
agent_relevance: Partial answer to gap 1: reasoning models improve systematicity on near-format analogy but not robustness to noisy input.

source: Gick & Holyoak (1983) Schema induction and analogical transfer, Exp 4
finding: Two analogous stories transfer better than one. Writing down what the two stories share builds a schema that predicts transfer.
numbers: Radiation problem. Two analogs (similar and dissimilar pooled) 45% convergence solution before hint vs 21% for one analog plus control story (G2(1)=6.35, p<.01); total 80 vs 53% (p<.003). N=28 two similar (39% before hint, 79% total), N=23 two dissimilar (52%, 83%), N=47 one analog (21%, 53%).
limits: Undergraduates, one problem (radiation), story-reading task. Similar vs dissimilar pair difference (52 vs 39%) not significant.
agent_relevance: Support for giving the agent two or more source cases and having it state their common structure before applying it (a compare-then-abstract step).

finding: Quality of the induced schema predicts transfer. Good schemas almost always led to the solution unprompted.
numbers: Of 30 two-analog subjects with scored schemas, 21% wrote good schemas, 20% intermediate, 59% poor (percentages as printed). Good schema: 91% (10 of 11) solved before the hint, none failed overall. Intermediate: 40% before hint, 90% total. Poor: 30% before, 70% total. G2(4)=15.8, p<.005.
limits: Correlational. Authors warn that skilled solvers may both write good schemas and solve better. Small cells. Table rows garbled in extraction; prose used.
agent_relevance: Abstraction quality, not mere exposure, is the active ingredient. An audit of the stated relation could be a gate before transfer.

source: Gick & Holyoak (1983) intro summarising Gick & Holyoak (1980) and replications
finding: Recap of the 1980 noticing result: analogy works when hinted but is rarely noticed unprompted.
numbers: About 75% of subjects with the appropriate military story produced the convergence solution after a hint vs under 10% of controls (irrelevant story or none). Without a hint after memorising the story, about 30%. With a 10% base rate, only a third or less of those who could use the analogy noticed it.
quote: only about 30% of our subjects produced the convergence solution, as opposed to about 75% who produced it when a hint was given
limits: This is the authors' own summary of 1980, not the 1980 paper itself (repository returned 403, Springer paywalled). Per-experiment Ns for 1980 not read.
agent_relevance: Confirms K17 numbers. Retrieval cue is the bottleneck: an explicit trigger such as 'what is this like?' is the analogue of the hint.

finding: Replication of the analogy advantage in a different problem with high-school students.
numbers: N=69 (25 recall, 24 summary, 20 control). Analog conditions 71% pendulum solution before hint vs 20% control (G2(1)=15.8, p<.001); total 98 vs 30% (G2(1)=30.1). Recall vs summary instructions did not differ (96 vs 100% total).
limits: Table rows garbled in extraction; numbers from the prose. Control base rate for this problem is 20-30%.
agent_relevance: Same pattern in a second problem: large gain once the analog is in play.

source: Gick & Holyoak (1983) Exp 2 and 3 (verbal principle, diagrams)
finding: Adding the abstract principle or a diagram to the story did not help spontaneous transfer.
numbers: Exp 2 (N=31/28/29): analog+principle 32% before hint, 80% total; analog only 29%, 79%; principle only 28%, 66%. Exp 3 (N=26/25/15): analog+diagrams 23%/81%; analog only 40%/76%; diagrams only 7%/67%.
limits: No difference significant. A stated abstraction alone did not beat the story.
agent_relevance: Caution for gap 5: a given abstraction alone did not raise unprompted transfer; self-induced schema from comparison did (d03).

source: Liu, Dubova, Conklin, Harada & Griffiths (2026) Serendipity by Design: cross-domain mappings and creativity in humans and LLMs
finding: A random cross-domain source helped humans but not LLMs on average. LLMs were already more original than humans without it.
numbers: 140 human generators, 7 LLMs (o3, Claude-Sonnet-4, gpt-4o, gemini-2.5-pro, deepseek-v3, Llama-3.3-70b, Qwen2.5-72B), 10 products, 2800 ideas rated by 1002 raters (preregistered). Humans cross-domain mean originality 2.93 vs user-need 2.57. o3 3.83, Claude-Sonnet-4 3.76. LLM overall cross-domain effect not significant.
limits: Product features, one task family, 5-point originality scale, preprint. Random sources, not matched ones.
agent_relevance: A source prompt is not free for strong models. Test per model; do not assume more analogy means more novelty.

source: Liu et al. (2026) Serendipity by Design: distance analysis
finding: The further the source, the more original the idea; strong LLMs only gain when the source is far. No inverted U was reported.
numbers: Wikipedia-based semantic distance predicts originality (humans beta=.1, t=2.72, p<.01; LLMs beta=.18, t=4.81, p<.001). For o3 and Claude-Sonnet-4 the cross-domain effect is 0.02 (p=.64) over all pairs, 0.12 (p=.029) on the top 50% most distant pairs, 0.24 (p=.024) on the top 10%. Pooled LLMs: cross-domain initially worse than user-need; gap closed after excluding the closest 20%.
limits: Everyday-object concept pairs only; originality outcome; subsetting by distance is post hoc.
agent_relevance: For gap 4: monotone far-is-better on originality for a strong LLM, with a floor distance below which a source hurts. Pick far sources and filter close ones; usefulness cost in d10.

source: Liu et al. (2026) Serendipity by Design: originality-usefulness tradeoff and transfer type
finding: Humans' most original cross-domain ideas lost usefulness; LLM ideas did not. Humans copied surface features, LLMs transferred function and structure.
numbers: Top 10% most original human ideas under cross-domain mapping matched LLMs on originality (beta=0.02, p=.63) but were rated less useful (difference 0.81, p<.001), less worth investing in (0.60, p<.001) and less feasible (0.26, p=.045). Example: pickle desk originality 4.78, utility 1.22.
limits: Coefficients as read from text; sign conventions follow the paper's mixed models.
agent_relevance: Structural transfer is the target; surface transfer gives vivid but useless ideas. Score utility next to novelty.

source: Shen, Druckmann & Zou (2026) Unlocking LLM Creativity in Science through Analogical Reasoning
finding: Explicit analogy generation (extract relational structure, search other domains, map back) beats a plain cross-domain prompt on diversity and novelty at the same 2 calls.
numbers: 50 biomedical problems, Claude Sonnet 4.5, GPT-5.2, Gemini 3 Flash, 150 generations per problem. Solution Vendi 5.81 (no-domain) and 8.34 (cross-domain); AR is 90-173% higher. About 5% of generated domains unique in baselines. Binary novelty Claude 1.6 < 21.6 < 50.4%, GPT 9.0 < 28.2 < 58.8%, Gemini 8.9 < 37.8 < 68.9% (no-domain < cross-domain < AR). AR 2 calls, cross-domain 2, no-domain 1. About 0.02 dollars per problem.
limits: LLM-judged novelty (agreement with humans 75.7%). Baseline is one prompt, not best-of-n at equal tokens. Biomedical only. Preprint.
agent_relevance: Gap 9: duplicate collapse is real in baselines (domain Vendi 2.64-2.84) and an analogy step that varies the source domain restores diversity. Also partial answer to gap 5: the relation-extraction step is part of the winning pipeline, though not ablated.

source: Shen et al. (2026) human preference study and analogy quality
finding: Humans prefer analogy-derived solutions as more novel but rate fewer as reasonable.
numbers: Pairwise: AR solution more novel 78% of the time (kappa .445). Reasonable: AR 67% vs cross-domain baseline 86% (kappa .155 vs .416). Domain Distance 6.99/6.83/7.53 for AR vs 2.29/3.08/3.37 no-domain (Claude/GPT/Gemini). Structural Depth 7.06-8.60 in all settings. Human-LLM judge agreement 88.6% for distance, 75.7% for novelty.
limits: Annotator count not extracted; low agreement on reasonableness for AR.
agent_relevance: Gap 6: about one third of far-analogy solutions judged unreasonable (33% vs 14% baseline). A feasibility audit stage is justified, but no audit was tested at equal tokens.

source: Zheng et al. (2023) Take a Step Back: Evoking Reasoning via Abstraction
finding: State the principle or abstract concept first, then reason. Large gains on physics, chemistry and time-sensitive QA.
numbers: PaLM-2L MMLU Physics 66.4 -> 73.2, Chemistry 70.9 -> 81.8; GPT-4 Physics 69.4 -> 84.5 (CoT 82.9), Chemistry 80.9 -> 85.6 (CoT 85.3). TimeQA PaLM-2L 41.5 -> 66.0 (RAG 57.4, step-back+RAG 68.7). SituatedQA 54.3 -> 57.5. Fixes 20.5% of baseline errors on MMLU Physics while adding 11.9% new ones; over 90% of its remaining errors are in the reasoning step, not the principle step.
limits: Abstraction of a single problem, not mapping across source and target. GPT-4 with CoT is close to step-back. No near-vs-far split. 5 runs, SDs reported.
agent_relevance: Outside ARN the abstraction step helps, but its edge over plain CoT on a strong model is small (84.5 vs 82.9) and it adds errors. Gap 5 answered only for single-problem abstraction.

source: Camposampiero et al. (2025) effort and token cost, o3-mini medium vs high
finding: Higher reasoning effort costs far more tokens and gives mixed gains on out-of-distribution analogy.
numbers: Task accuracy medium vs high across the three Table 1 columns: 86.6/77.6/81.0 at 5445/7884/7209 tokens vs 92.6/82.4/80.6 at 9867/19041/19449 tokens. Hardest condition 31.0% at 53596 tokens. Abstract: 3.4x more reasoning tokens while accuracy fell 86.6 -> 17.0.
limits: Token counts are averages; column definitions follow the paper's range settings.
agent_relevance: An equal-token control must be reported: on this task more tokens did not buy robustness.

source: Dunbar via Frontiers/PMC review (secondary) on in vivo analogy distance
finding: The review states that nearly all lab-meeting analogies were local or regional. It gives no counts.
numbers: 98% of analogies classified as local or regional (Dunbar 1995, 1997). No totals, no long-distance count, no count of analogies that led to discoveries.
limits: Secondary source only. The Dunbar chapters were not opened; the escholarship and per-central links returned non-matching files.
agent_relevance: Gap 8 stays open for exact counts, but the 98% within-field share fits the reading that distant analogy is rare in practice.

source: Search for agent-memory analogical retrieval (xMemory 2602.02007, Co-Need Index, GAAMA 2603.27910)
finding: Search snippets only: recent agent-memory papers argue similarity top-k collapses to redundant items and add structure (hierarchies, relation edges). None tests cross-domain structural analogy retrieval.
limits: Not opened; snippet level. Not analogy tests.
agent_relevance: Gap 7 stays open: no study found that retrieves an agent's own past tasks by purpose or mechanism and compares against similarity retrieval.

source: Search for reasoning-model reruns of Qin et al. and analogical prompting
finding: Two search phrasings found no 2025-2026 study that re-runs relevant-vs-random exemplars or analogical prompting on o1/R1-class models, and none with an equal-token comparison against extra sampling.
numbers: None found. Known earlier: Qin et al. Relevant or Random (2404.12728) says accuracy of self-generated examples matters, random can match relevant.
limits: Absence of evidence from at most 8 searches; arXiv, Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex APIs returned 429 during this run.
agent_relevance: Gaps 1 (verbal far analogy) and 3 stay open. Treat as an experiment for our own harness.
